beats.Meaning: Dawn in the Low. Ozzie throws Tavi and Reza off his couch in Blister 9 (a dead aerostatic freight blister at 110 meters) because his girl is moving in. Establish the two of them as nineteen, fresh out of basic education, no chrome, no skill, no plan, functionally identical: a garbage bag of stuff, standing on the catwalk. Ground the Low: ungoverned aerostatic band, altitude equals class, the Thread on the southern horizon going up forever. Comedy of two nobodies at rock bottom who are somehow not crushed; establish their warmth and the high-five (they high-five even now, defiant and stupid). End on them looking at the Thread and deciding, without saying it yet, that down is not the only direction. POV anchored on Tavi; Reza rendered from beside him.
beats.Subtext: The Thread (up) is the whole arc in one image; the high-five is the token whose slow death is the story. Reza already reads a room a half-second faster than Tavi.

beats.Meaning: Over cadged noodles on Skillet Row, the boys decide, with total unearned confidence, to become operators. No skills, no chrome, and the one asset they have: no aversion to violence they have ever had to test. They go to Scraps at her noodle booth, the lowest door of the trade. She sizes them up, unimpressed, and hands them the scrap-job nobody wants: remind a delinquent debtor he is a debtor. Base rate, standard, no advance, no sympathy; a number that is nothing to her and sounds like a fortune to them. Establish Scraps as the on-ramp and the cycle. The boys leave thrilled, with no idea what they just agreed to.
beats.Subtext: Scraps has watched a thousand kids take this job and not come back; she treats these two exactly the same. The no-aversion-to-violence line is a loaded gun.

beats.Meaning: The first job, a comedy of errors: wrong door, wrong floor, a panic, a plan that was never a plan. It goes wrong every possible way until Reza, cornered and terrified, improvises real violence: body-true, ugly, specific; the actual physics of hurting a person who is bigger than expected, and how it does not feel the way the Volume feeds said it would. Tavi improvises a fumbled system-fix while Reza covers with a lie, and between dumb luck and a half-second of attention, they complete the objective just enough. They barely escape. Warmth and ultraviolence in one beat: they are laughing and shaking at once. The debtor is reminded; the boys are changed and do not know it yet.
beats.Subtext: Reza's secret is planted here: the first time he really hurt someone it did not horrify him. Neither says this. Tavi sees it and never says so either.

beats.Meaning: Scraps pays them the base rate onto a credstick. They look at the number and lose their minds: WHOA, we are RICH. It is not much; to them it is everything. The best, dumbest, purest high-five of the story. Immediately they plan to blow all of it, tonight, on booze and drugs and girls, the only thing either of them has ever imagined doing with money. Render the specific joy of the first money you ever earned with your own hands and a little blood. Let it be genuinely happy; the story earns its later ache by meaning this.
beats.Subtext: The plan to blow it all is the fork the whole story turns on. This is the peak of them being identical.

beats.Meaning: On the very cusp of blowing everything (credstick out, night ahead) Tavi has a flicker of something neither of them has ever had: a want with a future in it. He says it small: or we do it again. The hinge of the story, consumption turning into intention. They argue, they laugh, they almost do not, and then they reinvest instead of incinerate. The first adult decision either of them has made. Keep it unsentimental and funny; it is not a montage-swelling moment, it is two idiots choosing, barely, to become people.
beats.Subtext: First time Tavi leads and Reza follows, a preview of the divergence. Tavi's first real want is also the seed of who he becomes without Reza.

beats.Meaning: A slightly bigger job. They are still amateurs, but each has learned exactly one thing, and it shows. For the first time their natural lanes appear: Reza wants the front, the doorway, his body between the danger and the work; Tavi wants the wire, the angle, the thing you switch off. It goes better (not clean, but better) and they feel, for the first time, the specific pleasure of being good at something on purpose. Establish the competence high that will later become the thing that separates them. First taste of a reputation.
beats.Subtext: The lanes that make them a great team are the same lanes that will make them two different men. The reader should feel the pleasure without yet feeling the cost.

beats.Meaning: With real money now, the boys buy their first chrome from a Low clinic: Reza takes subdermal armor and the start of muscle and reflex; Tavi takes a splice jack behind the ear. Render the body-true reality of cheap cyberware: the surgery, the wrongness, the days of the body arguing with the hardware, the specific new sense of it under the skin. On the same payday they buy the matched twins: two identical cheap Meridian Ankle-Biter holdout pistols, because being armed the same is a way of saying we are the same. The chrome sorts them physically for the first time: one built to take a hit, one built to disappear.
beats.Subtext: The twins are the Chekhov subplot; they buy the SAME gun on purpose. The chrome choices are the divergence made surgical: Reza external and felt, Tavi internal and hidden.

beats.Meaning: Flush and freshly chromed, the boys go to the Honeycomb, a BTL den, and jack into The Glass. In the hyperreal haze two women, Sunday and Ivet, become transcendent, angels, proof the boys have arrived. Adult, body-true, consensual sex rendered with real adult reactions: the involuntary physical responses, the specific sensation, not euphemism and not pornography; the frame is literary authenticity, what a body actually feels, heightened by the drug and the Glass. Between beds the boys high-five across the gap, delirious, certain they are in love. Keep both women people, not props, even inside the boys' delusion. This is the top of the come-up's pleasure; let it be genuinely good so the morning can be genuinely sad.
beats.Subtext: Everything transcendent here is the boys' own chemistry and hype; the women are more real than the boys can see while jacked. The high-five here is drunk and hollow-in-waiting.

beats.Meaning: Sober and un-jacked in grey morning light, the boys see the night for what it was: Sunday and Ivet are not angels, they are tired, strung-out, ordinary people managing a bad economy with the only currency the Low left them. The disillusion belongs to the boys and to the hyperreality, not to the women; grant the women their dignity: one small, real human exchange (Sunday says the true small thing; Ivet leaves first, practical, already gone) that the boys cannot un-see. Out of shame and discomfort rather than contempt comes the first real want of their lives: not this. They decide to upgrade (better jobs, better nights, better everything), the first time either of them has wanted better on purpose. Ambition crystallizes out of disappointment.
beats.Subtext: True midpoint: the pleasure was fake, the want it produces is real. Upgrade is the engine of the back half and the thing that pulls them to different altitudes. No contempt for the women; the shame is the boys'.

beats.Meaning: The boys buckle down and specialize hard, and on one real job they each earn their handle on-page. Reza holds a doorway alone against a crew while Tavi works: a genuine ultraviolent set piece, body-true, the wall doing what a wall does, and someone calls him Rampart and it sticks. Tavi, meanwhile, kills a whole system clean: alarms, idents, lights, the noise of a place gone dark at his hand, and someone calls him Cutout. They come out the far side booked as a package, Rampart and Cutout, a wall and a ghost sold together, the best product on a fixer's board. Peak of the duo. The best real high-five. Their first jobs above the Low; the altitude starts to climb.
beats.Subtext: The summit they will spend the rest of the story descending from, not into failure but into separation. The handles that make them somebody are the names of two different things.

beats.Meaning: Auda Vane, the mid-tier fixer they graduated to, has a job that needs a ghost and no wall: precision, no noise, no room for Rampart. She books Tavi alone. It is not a snub; it is just the job, and Tavi knows it, and takes it, and it goes clean, and he feels a small unforgivable relief at working without the weight of covering Reza. Meanwhile Reza waits, bored, left behind, too big for a job that has no door to hold. The first crack, unspoken on both sides. Neither of them names it because naming it would make it real.
beats.Subtext: Tavi's secret lands here: the relief is the thing he cannot forgive himself, more than any of Reza's later bailing. The package has its first seam, and Auda Vane already saw it coming.

beats.Meaning: The reverse of beat 11. Reza ditches a shared depot job for Coeli and the Volume arena; Tavi covers it alone, and the old reflex - the certainty that Reza has the right side of the doorway - simply is not there. Tavi goes left; the guard comes from Reza's side; Tavi takes a real wound: two ribs, one cracked clean, one flexed. He patches himself alone in the dark and says nothing; Reza will not know for days. When they finally talk it is cold; not a screaming fight, worse, a quiet one, two people being careful with each other for the first time. The break is real now.
beats.Subtext: Reza did nothing evil; he has a life now, which is exactly the tragedy. The wound is the friendship's, worn on Tavi's body. Coeli is not a villain, just the direction Reza was already going.

beats.Meaning: They are working separately now: different altitudes, different circles, different chrome philosophies, different everything. They try, once, to hang out like the old days, and it just does not work: the jokes land a half-beat off, there is nothing to say, the silences are not the old comfortable ones. The high-five gets attempted and it is mistimed, hollow, an artifact of two people they used to be. Show the specific grief of outgrowing someone while you are both still alive and still fond. The twins: Reza long since upgraded to serious hardware, his Ankle-Biter in a drawer somewhere; Tavi still carries his. Nothing dramatic happens. That is the point.
beats.Subtext: The emotional floor. The friendship is not ending in a blowup; it is just over, the way a phase is over. Tavi carrying the twin is the whole subplot paying off quietly.

beats.Meaning: Auda Vane, without ceremony or malice, stops booking Rampart-and-Cutout as a package and books them as two separate operators: the administrative fact that formally ends the partnership, external and undramatic, the market simply pricing what they have become. A last meeting: cordial, genuinely fond, and done. Reza lands the theme not as a speech but as an image and one small true sentence, that some friendships are for a phase of a life, and outgrowing one is grief, and it is also the shape of becoming yourself. They part in literally different directions: Reza rises, up-altitude, into the bright tiers on an eigenlift, the flashy life he became; Tavi walks the mid-levels toward his next quiet job. Final image, avalanche and no epilogue: Tavi passes Scraps at her booth on Skillet Row and sees two new nobodies taking the scrap-job, the cycle turning again. He does not high-five anyone. He goes to work, more himself than he has ever been. It is sad. It is okay.
beats.Subtext: The external resolution is Auda's booking, not a decision by either boy; per the blueprint, no internal-peace ending. The closing cycle (Scraps plus two new nobodies) says this story is one turn of a wheel. Reza not high-fiving is the subplot's last note.
